title: Playing by ear and the Tuxedo band's 'Nella' joke
summary: They played by ear for gut-bucket dances, with blues like St. Louis Blues and a comic break in a tune that made audiences shout.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Did you ever play anything by ear at all? Without reading from the music? Did you ever play anything by ear at all? Without reading from the music?

Plenty of time. You did plenty of time. You did plenty of time. You know we used to make those wagging at the time and give them things like that. That's why we couldn't use no music at that time. No. You know we'd buck. You know we'd come on to some time, bands would buck for about a half an hour you know. And like that but you couldn't use no music there. You had the gut bucket. Because most of it was anything you could do, anything you could move.
What pieces did you play then?

Well most of those they've come to places like there was something. They played plenty of blues you know like St. Louis Blues. Nella was one of our main hosts. The other bands couldn't play it. They didn't know how we got it you see. Of course that was the number we fixed. The piece of music was Nella, that was the name of it. Well we cut the name off you see. And Tom Burton, we used to play a reggae and one night we were always playing, had a good crowd of people playing color dance. They had a couple of drinks in them. And we used to make a break in that hooey and Nella you know. We made the... We stopped there. And so he started to have drunk one night. And so when we made that break he said... We said oooey. And we kept that up.
And we made it. And made it.

And made it. And he got laughed over and sat so many times. Yeah. She made it. And he said oooey. And the people who didn't know. We just had to play. And nobody know where it comes from. What else was going to do. They never did know how to play. And we kept like that's the last job. And that's the moment we kept in the job all the time. And we used to play that. And that was a scream. And none of them couldn't play. And then the...
That was the Silver Leaf that did that.
Oh. That was the original Tuxedo band.
